summary: Learn field-based erosion assessment, treatment prioritization and watershed monitoring. Explore the five-day intermediate course.
lede: Erosion control training helps watershed officers, soil-conservation practitioners and catchment planners prioritize erosion treatments. Participants map sediment sources and downstream routes, use RUSLE for screening, and distinguish slope, gully and channel processes when selecting feasible measures. They document conservation options with the WOCAT approach and develop monitoring indicators and a sequenced watershed action plan.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who assess soil loss, plan watershed interventions or monitor erosion-control work across catchments.
outcomes: Costed Watershed Rehabilitation and Dashboard Planning
RUSLE Annual Sheet and Rill Erosion Estimation
Sediment Control and Water-Quality Monitoring Planning
prerequisites: Prior experience in watershed, land, agriculture, soil conservation or environmental field work is recommended. No coding or programming is required. The course treats RUSLE as a screening method and does not train you to produce engineering construction specifications.
